title: The Danger of Being Spiritually Busy — Luke 10:41
paragraphs: The Danger of Being Spiritually Busy — Luke 10:41
That should shake every spiritually busy heart.

In Luke 10:41, Jesus tells Martha, “You are anxious and troubled about many things.” Not because service is evil. Not because preparation is sin. But because it is possible to be active around Jesus while neglecting intimacy with Jesus.

You can fill your calendar with ministry.
Answer messages.
Lead worship.
Preach sermons.
Serve the poor.
Show up at every church event.
And still be inwardly restless, distracted, dry, and distant from the voice of Christ.

Martha was not in a nightclub.
She was not rebelling.
She was in the house.
Serving.
But her hands were full while her heart was troubled.
And that is where this cuts deep for many of us.

Because spiritual busyness can look holy on the outside while hiding anxiety, pride, people-pleasing, and a quiet refusal to simply sit at His feet. We start confusing motion with devotion. Activity with obedience. Exhaustion with faithfulness.

Jesus did not shame Martha.
He invited her back.

Back to the “one thing necessary.”
Back to presence before performance.
Back to communion before contribution.
Back to being with Him before doing for Him.

This is the Gospel.
Jesus did not come merely to make workers out of us.
He came to reconcile us to God through His blood, forgive our sins, and bring us near. We are not saved by how much we do for Christ. We are saved by what Christ has done for us on the cross and in the empty tomb. From that grace, true service flows.

You do not have to prove your love to Jesus by burning yourself out.
You do not have to earn His smile with endless religious motion.
Repent of the rush.
Come back to His feet.
Choose the better portion.

Busy is not always faithful.
Sometimes the holiest thing you can do is be still enough to listen.
